details.title_candidate: Broiled Walnut-Mustard Salmon with Asparagus and Brown Rice
details.flavour_profile: Nutty, tangy, and bright with a caramelized crust

warnings: Stage 4 coverage: 'Extra-virgin olive oil': [748608] Oil, olive, extra virgin has no USDA value for fiber_g, protein_g (which would be summed as zero) — switched to [171413] Oil, olive, salad or cooking.

details.summary: This is a superb, flawlessly executed recipe. It delivers a highly appetizing, nutrient-dense meal using smart techniques and convenient ingredients that completely honor the 30-minute promise and dietary guidelines.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is excellent and classic. The mustard and lemon provide a bright, tangy contrast to the rich salmon and walnuts, while the asparagus adds an earthy baseline. Very well balanced.
All ingredients are fully accounted for in the instructions, and salt and pepper are properly divided between the two components.

The steps are comprehensive. You provide a time range for broiling (6 to 8 minutes), a check-in time (6 minutes), and excellent visual cues for doneness for all three items on the pan (asparagus tender, walnuts toasted, salmon flaking).
Perfectly aligns with a Modern American / Mediterranean style, focusing on lean proteins, whole grains, nuts, and fresh vegetables.

Broiling works beautifully for both asparagus and salmon. Using the wet mustard mixture to adhere the walnuts helps protect the nuts from burning under the direct heat, though the instruction to check at 6 minutes is a smart, necessary precaution.

The macros map cleanly to the ingredients. The ~43g of carbohydrate makes sense between the 250g brown rice pouch and the 16 oz of asparagus, and the saturated fat reflects the healthy fats from the salmon and walnuts without breaking the ceiling.

The title is accurate and the intro is inviting. 'Liver-supporting omega-3s' is an acceptable phrase as it doesn't cross into the banned 'cure' or 'detox' territory, keeping the tone practical and realistic.
Highly appealing. The textural contrast between the crunchy walnuts, tender salmon, and crisp asparagus makes this a deeply satisfying weeknight meal.
A textbook example of eating for both conditions: it features a whole-grain carb for blood sugar control alongside a lean protein, healthy fats, and a large vegetable portion for liver health.

Added sugar is completely zero. The recipe includes a robust, high-quality complex carbohydrate (brown rice) that confidently places the dish in the required 32-55g window without relying on refined grains.
Fits the 'Fish & Seafood Dinners' intent perfectly. It provides the targeted omega-3s in an ultra-fast weeknight format and hits all the macro targets for a 'main' dish.
Easily achieved in under 30 minutes. Prep is minimal, broiling takes less than 10 minutes, and the microwave rice pouch is exactly the kind of first-class, realistic shortcut this book encourages.
